title: Two localization-normalized derived pullback tensor identifications
statement:
Let $g:\mathscr X'\to\mathscr X$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe, let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathscr X$, let $S$ be one on $\mathscr X'$, and specify $c:R=g^{-1}B\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Let $t\in\Gamma(B)$, write $t'=g^{-1}t$, $s=c(t')$, $V=B[1/t]$, $R_t=R[1/t']$, and $U=S[1/s]$, using sheaf localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Use module sheaves, sheaf tensors, unbounded derived categories and ringed derived pullback [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. For every $K\in D(B)$ there are natural isomorphisms in $D(U)$
$$a_K:U\otimes_S^L(S\otimes_R^L g^{-1}K)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\otimes_R^L g^{-1}K,$$
$$b_K:U\otimes^L_{g^{-1}V}g^{-1}(V\otimes_B^L K)\xrightarrow{\sim}U\otimes_R^L g^{-1}K.$$
Here $g^{-1}V\cong R_t$ is the canonical localization-unit-preserving identification of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]; no invertibility or flatness of $c$ is assumed. More precisely, for any flat-term K-flat resolution $T^\bullet\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $N=g^{-1}T^\bullet$. The complexes $N$, $S\otimes_RN$, $R_t\otimes_RN$, and their scalar extensions to $U$ are flat-term K-flat over their respective coefficient sheaves. Under the canonical derived computation comparisons, $a_K$ and $b_K$ are represented by the sheafifications of the chain isomorphisms
$$u\otimes(v\otimes n)\longmapsto uv\otimes n,\qquad u\otimes(r/(t')^m\otimes n)\longmapsto u\,c(r)s^{-m}\otimes n,$$
respectively, and both inverse maps send $u\otimes n$ to $u\otimes(1\otimes n)$. These formulas include all balancing and fraction relations, commute with differentials, and determine the same derived comparisons for every choice of resolution. Both comparisons are natural for every derived morphism $K\to L$.

proof.text: Construct the localized coefficient map sectionwise by the universal property of Localization.Away. The target localization unit makes the image of the source section invertible. Uniqueness glues the sectionwise maps; naturality of sheafification gives e and its unit equation. The universal-property formula on fractions gives the displayed equation, including zero divisors and the zero ring.

Use the scalar-extension/inverse-image adjunction comparison on independently sized sites. Its hypotheses are precisely the commuting unit square hIt. The unit equation, inverse-image compatibility with scalar multiplication and the scalar-extension unit formula give the generalized pure-tensor equation for gamma. This uses no claim that global pure tensors generate all sections.

Geometric inverse image preserves K-flatness by the independent-universe pullback proof and preserves termwise flatness by its flatness theorem. Applying the ringed K-flat pullback theorem to the identity geometric inverse image gives scalar-extension preservation. These statements apply successively to all eight complexes, without flatness hypotheses on the coefficient maps.

Localize the full subcategory of the homotopy category consisting of flat-term K-flat complexes. K-flat resolutions provide the required resolving-class localization. For the two derived composite functors, the universal scalar-extension counits and exact inverse-image comparison are isomorphisms on this subcategory. Whisker gamma with the homotopy quotient and the derived quotient, conjugate by these computation isomorphisms, and lift it through fully faithful precomposition with the resolving-class localization. Its preimage is a natural isomorphism q with the required computation equation.

For a, whisker the existing normalized derived scalar-tower comparison by geometric inverse image. For b, first whisker q by extension along e, then compose with the same normalized scalar-tower comparison for R to R_t to U and transport along the coefficient-map equality. The scalar-tower representative equation, naturality at the exact inverse-image computation map, and naturality of the last extension counit prove both displayed representative equations. These are natural isomorphisms on the whole derived category, so naturality includes every derived morphism and resolution independence is automatic.

That lemma needs flat terms only, never a flat ring map. Step 2: e:R_t→U via the sectionwise localization-away universal property and sheafification; the fraction relations check out even with zero divisors. Steps 3-4: I checked the inner and outer balancing, the inverses and both composites; they are elementary uses of the sheaf bilinear universal property. Step 5: localization-inverse-image-coherence gives g^{-1}(V⊗_B T)≅R_t⊗_R N with the units preserved, and ringed-topoi-derived-pullback computes all three derived sides. U⊗_R is the same R-algebra on both routes because e(r/1)=c(r). Step 6: degree-zero coefficients, so no Koszul sign; commutation with d, chain-map and homotopy naturality hold. Step 7: only the localization-equivalence clause of site-derived-tensor-descent is used, plus localization-universal-property (2)/(3) for descent, independence of resolution and naturality for all derived morphisms. proof_deps equals the union of uses. Edge cases tested: t nilpotent, t=1, g=id with c=id, R=Z with S=Z/2 and t=3 (c not flat), K=0. The 8 tool_uses are generic black boxes and are accepted. No SGA. lean.note: The two comparisons are natural isomorphisms in D(U), tied by explicit equations through universal computation counits to the ordinary balanced tensor comparisons. The localized inverse image is presented after the canonical localization-unit-preserving ring identification. Helpers specialize the existing universal coefficient-extension presentations and normalization laws; no alternative tensor, derived category or inverse-image construction is introduced. FlatK abbreviates the two recorded predicates, and fraction is the sheafification image of an actual Localization.Away element. Added the three already landed interface nodes used in the signature.
